{{Quote|The big-mouth running the show claimed he was Tarro Blood. He's a big shot even for a Mandalorian.|Mako|<ref name="TOR:TLF" />}}
'''Tarro Blood''' was a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]]-turned [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] who operated during the [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]] and the [[Galactic War]] between the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]]. He was a competitor in the [[Great Hunt (competition)|Great Hunt]], going to great lengths in order to sabotage his fellow competitors.

==History==
===First Great Hunt===
{{Quote|Tarro Blood? I've heard of you. Nearly got crippled by the other Mandalorians at the Great Hunt ten years back.|Braden|<ref name="TOR:TLF" />}}
The son of [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaanian]] nobility, Tarro Blood renounced his claim as the heir to a minor lordship in favor of pursuing greater glory and fame as a galaxy-renowned [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenary]].<ref name="TOR:TB" />

Leaving his past behind and taking on a new dramatic moniker, Blood was able to prove that he was no pretender after years of training under the famed Mandalorian champion,<ref name="TOR:TB" /> [[Hedarr Soongh]].<ref name="TOR:HR">{{TORcite|type=class|Bounty Hunter|Honor Regained|Nar Shaddaa}}</ref> Under the guidance of this exceptional tutor, Blood became a feared warrior and the favorite to claim victory in the [[Great Hunt (c. 3653 BBY)|next Great Hunt]].<ref name="TOR:TB" />

Unfortunately for him, Tarro Blood's characteristic arrogance and sudden rise to prominence rubbed his competition the wrong way. The other Mandalorians in the competition made it their mission to ensure that he never came close to claiming victory. The resulting defeat nearly cost Blood his life, in addition to his pride, and he remained out of the public eye for nearly a decade, choosing not to participate in the next Great Hunt.<ref name="TOR:TB" /> In fact, Tarro spent the next years building up support with the Mandalorians, allowing him to be eventually considered as a Mandalorian and get easier access to the next Great Hunts.<ref name="TOR:BC">{{TORcite|type=class|Bounty Hunter|Big Chief|Hutta}}</ref>

===Second Great Hunt===
{{Quote|Winning the Great Hunt won't merely be good--it will be splendid. When I win, the entire galaxy will know the name Tarro Blood--and I'll charge extravagant fees for my services.|Tarro Blood|<ref name="TOR:TLF" />}}
[[File:Braden_killed.jpg|thumb|left|270px|Sedyn Kyne kills Braden and Jory]]
After ten years, Blood entered [[Great Hunt (c. 3643 BBY)|another Hunt]], and had no desire to maintain honor during the competition, sabotaging his competitors at every chance. One of the rival hunters he targeted was [[Braden]], who had found a [[Hunter (individual)|talented protege]] to be a Great Hunt competitor. While the Hunter was out collecting a bounty on the [[Corellian/Legends|Corellian]] fugitive [[Vexx]], Blood confronted Braden and his friend [[Jory]], boasting that he intended to win the Great Hunt by eliminating his non-Mandalorian rivals, including a [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]] [[Vibroblade/Legends|vibroblade]] master from [[Ord Mantell/Legends|Ord Mantell]] and a [[Chiss/Legends|Chiss]] droid builder fond of explosives. Jory retorted that his plot had already failed, as the young bounty hunter was not present. However, Blood smugly corrected that he was aware of the competition rules barring him from killing his rivals before the allotted hour, vaguely claiming he simply eliminated them as threats. He then walked away as his accomplice, [[Sedyn Kyne]], murder Braden and his friend [[Jory]], unaware that his actions were on holocam, in order to strand the Hunter on [[Nal Hutta/Legends|Nal Hutta]].<ref name="TOR:TLF" /> He later dispatched a [[Rodian/Legends|Rodian]] bounty hunter named [[Nails]] to take down the Hunter, promising to get her into the Great Hunt, but his lackey greatly underestimated her opponent and was killed.<ref name="TOR:SA">{{TORcite|type=class|Bounty Hunter|Settling Accounts|Hutta}}</ref>

The Hunter managed to win sponsorship into the Great Hunt from [[Suudaa Nem'ro]]<ref name="TOR:MS">{{TORcite|type=class|Bounty Hunter|My Sponsorship|Hutta}}</ref> and arrived on [[Dromund Kaas/Legends|Dromund Kaas]] to win a spot in the final melee.<ref name="TOR:TH">{{TORcite|type=class|Bounty Hunter|The Huntmaster|Dromund Kaas}}</ref> Blood continued to interfere by hiring freelance Imperial soldiers lead by Sergeant [[Wallax]] to interrupt the Hunter's first bounty at the [[Nexus Room]] [[Cantina/Legends|Cantina]]. Blood then called Wallax directly to check in and was disappointed to find that the Sergeant was in the process of confronting the Hunter. Wallax ended the holocall, promising to talk to Blood later, only for him and his squad to be killed by the Hunter.<ref name="TOR:AMT">{{TORcite|type=class|Bounty Hunter|A Musty Trail|Dromund Kaas}}</ref> 

Blood would later falsely tell the Great Hunt officials that the Hunter had perished to get the final melee started without them, only for his rival to show up just in time and kill all the other contenders.<ref name="TOR:TSG">{{TORcite|type=class|Bounty Hunter|The Spy Game|Dromund Kaas}}</ref> Deciding to directly intervene, Blood interrupted the [[Huntmaster (Wookiee)|Huntmaster]]'s speech, prompting the Hunter to draw their blaster on him, only for Huntmaster Assistant [[Lek]] to forbid any unsanctioned kills. Boasting that his rival's reckless act was the perfect example, Blood tried to denounce the Hunter's credentials, saying they were falsified by Mako, referring to her as a "little gutter rat of a sidekick". To his frustration, Lek declared they were aware of the Hunter's history but the Huntmaster had already made his decision. Infuriated at having failed to eliminate the Hunter from the competition, Blood vowed to complain to [[Mandalore the Vindicated]] and promised that he would have the Hunter's skull in his hand by the time the Great Hunt was finished.<ref name="TOR:TM" /> He then alerted the Imperial authorities that the Hunter intended to steal a [[D5-Mantis Patrol Craft]] from the [[Dromund Kaas spaceport|local spaceport]]; given the Great Hunt's history of stealing starships, the spaceport commander proclaimed Blood as a "good" Mandalorian. Despite this, the Hunter killed the Imperial squad and the [[Neimoidian/Legends|Neimoidian]] [[Unidentified smuggler (Dromund Kaas)|smuggler]] the ship belonged to, before departing Dromund Kaas in the D5-Mantis.<ref name="TOR:JR">{{TORcite|type=class|Bounty Hunter|Joy Ride|Dromund Kaas}}</ref>

Throughout the Great Hunt, Blood made constant interference in the Hunter's hunts. On [[Balmorra/Legends|Balmorra]], he tricked Vexx's siblings [[Vorr (Corellian)|Vorr]] and [[Vye]] into thinking that the Hunter shot Vexx in the back and killed Braden when he discovered the "crime."<ref name="TOR:PA">{{TORcite|type=class|Bounty Hunter|Pirrell's Ambitions|Balmorra}}</ref> On [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]], he then alerted Hunt target [[Gault Rennow|Tyresius Lokai]] that the Hunter was after him.<ref name="TOR:TTT">{{TORcite|type=class|Bounty Hunter|The Tatooine Target|the D5-Mantis}}</ref> On [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]], Blood paid off [[House Rist]] to assassinate the hunter.<ref name="TOR:KfaD">{{TORcite|type=class|Bounty Hunter|Kingmaker for a Day|Alderaan}}</ref> Blood also leaked the list of Great Hunt targets to sell on an auction on Hutta, forcing Assistant Huntsmaster [[Lek]] to call on the Hunter for assistance.<ref name="TOR:ADA">{{TORcite|type=class|Bounty Hunter|A Dangerous Auction|Dromund Kaas}}</ref>

The veteran [[Hedarr Soongh]] eventually became aware of Blood's crimes and assisted the Hunter in taking out Blood's allies on [[Nar Shaddaa/Legends|Nar Shaddaa]]. Soongh challenged Sedyn Kyne to a [[Taung blood duel]] against the Hunter. Kyne lost, but his compatriots fatally wounded Soongh when they refused his demand to stop persecuting the Hunter, but were subsequently killed by the Hunter, thus depriving Blood of any support in the Hunt.<ref name="TOR:HR" />

[[File:Tarro_Blood_in_cell.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Tarro Blood begs the Hunter to release him from the cell.]]
The final target of the Great Hunt was Jedi Master [[Kellian Jarro]], credited for the highest number of Mandalorian deaths. Blood was the first hunter to reach Jarro but was quickly subdued by a [[Mind trick/Legends|mind trick]]. Held under questioning, Blood claimed that the Hunter was his accomplice, hoping that the Republic would detain or at least kill his rival once and for all. He was wrong on both counts. Face-to-face for the last time, separated by a forcefield, Blood attempted to goad the Hunter into releasing him and facing him for a final confrontation, claiming that both Soongh and Braden would've wanted it. [[Mako (slicer)|Mako]], the Hunter's partner, stated that Braden would've wanted to see Blood as he was, undeserving of a warrior's death.<ref name="TOR:TMK" />

==Behind the scenes==
Tarro Blood is a non-player character from the massively multi-player online role playing game ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]'' released by [[BioWare]] in [[2011]]. He is voiced by [[Fred Tatasciore]].<ref name="TOR:TLF" />

Blood's fate can be decided three ways: leaving him in his cell to die when the ship is vaporized, freeing him from his cell to fight him in a stand up duel and kill him, or freeing him from his cell and shooting him immediately.<ref name="TOR:TMK" />
